reviewerName: Codex delegated adjudicator; economical cross-review Luna + Sol
note: Explicit AI-assisted editorial decision under owner delegation, after independent Luna and Sol full reviews. Every source, EN/VI target, option/explanation and transfer checked. Resolved prior follow-up ambiguity and Vietnamese overclaim. Original provider outputs and all edits retained. No human certification, learning outcome claim or deployment approval.

criteria.prompt: Original/permitted source, author, distribution rights and no learner PII checked.
criteria.evidence: Sol: Provenance identifies an AI-assisted original project reading, permits generation/distribution, and discloses no copied examination passage or learner PII. The generic receptionist scenario contains no personal data; rights judgment relies on that supplied provenance. Luna: Candidate declares an original AI-assisted project source, distribution permission, and no learner PII; review relies on this provenance statement.

criteria.prompt: Phrase occurs in cited source and the contextual sense is supported.
criteria.evidence: Sol: s1 contains hand over verbatim. Passing booking records to the next shift supports the transfer sense; no physical hand-position reading fits the object and recipient. Luna: s1 contains exact phrase ‘hand over’; the receptionist transfers booking records to the night team.

criteria.prompt: English gloss is the actual contextual meaning, not a selection rationale.
criteria.evidence: Sol: Giving documents or responsibility accurately describes this contextual transfer. The gloss permits either documents or responsibility and does not require a formal ceremony. Luna: Giving documents or responsibility to another person/team accurately describes passing booking records to the next shift.

criteria.prompt: Vietnamese gloss is accurate, natural and includes diacritics.
criteria.evidence: Sol: Bàn giao is natural Vietnamese with correct diacritics for shift-to-shift records/responsibility. Luna: ‘bàn giao’ is a natural, accurate Vietnamese gloss with diacritics.

criteria.prompt: Phrase occurs in cited source and the contextual sense is supported.
criteria.evidence: Sol: s2 contains follow up on verbatim; unresolved guest requests require subsequent checking/action, not following a person spatially. Luna: s2 contains exact phrase ‘follow up on’; requests unresolved during the day require later action.

criteria.prompt: English gloss is the actual contextual meaning, not a selection rationale.
criteria.evidence: Sol: Checking and taking further action on unfinished matters matches the unresolved-request context. This is a contextual gloss rather than a claim that all follow-up concerns unfinished tasks. Luna: Checking and taking further action on unfinished matters accurately fits the unresolved requests.

criteria.prompt: Vietnamese gloss is accurate, natural and includes diacritics.
criteria.evidence: Sol: Theo dõi và xử lý tiếp naturally conveys continued attention/action and has correct diacritics. Luna: ‘theo dõi và xử lý tiếp’ naturally captures monitoring and continuing action; diacritics are present.

criteria.prompt: Identify correct option and explain each distractor. No other plausible answer; no subjective style/intent assumptions.
criteria.evidence: Sol: q1 a is the contextual answer: records pass to the night team, with ordinary shift responsibility implied. b hiding is opposite; c cancellation does not mean transfer. Hidden/cancelled records could be events elsewhere, but neither paraphrases s1. Luna: a uniquely matches giving records/responsibility to the night team; b reverses transfer; c cancels records rather than transferring them.

criteria.prompt: Every option explanation is accurate; grammar/collocation claims are not overgeneralized.
criteria.evidence: Sol: q1 a accurately relates documents/responsibility to the handover; b and c explanations correctly distinguish hiding and cancellation. Overall explanation correctly centers passing records to the next team. Luna: Each option explanation correctly identifies the transfer, opposite action, or unrelated cancellation; overall rationale is accurate.

criteria.prompt: Identify correct option and explain each distractor. No other plausible answer; no subjective style/intent assumptions.
criteria.evidence: Sol: q2 a is grammatical and idiomatic. b before leaves lacks the subject needed for a finite clause; before leaving repairs it. c hand overs after will has an invalid inflection. No reasonable workplace context licenses these exact sentence forms. Luna: a is natural. b’s ‘before leaves’ is malformed because it lacks a subject after before (or should be ‘before leaving’); c has inflected ‘overs’ after modal will.

criteria.prompt: Every option explanation is accurate; grammar/collocation claims are not overgeneralized.
criteria.evidence: Sol: q2 a correctly identifies verb and to-recipient construction; b gives a valid local repair to leaving (before the assistant leaves is also possible, not excluded); c correctly restores base-form hand over after will. Overall sole grammatical answer claim holds. Luna: Option explanations correctly diagnose the malformed clause and modal bare-form error. They do not overstate the correction.

criteria.prompt: Identify correct option and explain each distractor. No other plausible answer; no subjective style/intent assumptions.
criteria.evidence: Sol: q3 b matches revisiting unresolved requests. a ignoring them and c making a first request do not convey follow-up, even if those actions could occur in another situation. Luna: b matches checking unresolved requests and acting on them. a is the opposite; c means initiating rather than continuing an existing request.

criteria.prompt: Every option explanation is accurate; grammar/collocation claims are not overgeneralized.
criteria.evidence: Sol: q3 explanations accurately contrast ignoring and a new first request against further attention/action to existing requests; the overall explanation is supported by unresolved during the day. Luna: All three rationales accurately distinguish ignoring, continued action, and a new request.

criteria.prompt: Identify correct option and explain each distractor. No other plausible answer; no subjective style/intent assumptions.
criteria.evidence: Sol: q4 a is natural. b on tomorrow morning adds an inappropriate preposition before this time expression; c will follows incorrectly inflects the modal complement. A different complaint context does not cure either form. Luna: a is correct. b adds an invalid ‘on’ before ‘tomorrow morning’; c uses ‘follows’ after modal will. Neither is a plausible standard sentence.

criteria.prompt: Every option explanation is accurate; grammar/collocation claims are not overgeneralized.
criteria.evidence: Sol: q4 a correctly uses follow up on; b deletion of on before tomorrow morning and c follows to follow are accurate local corrections. The overall answer claim does not depend on assumed intentions. Luna: b’s explanation correctly removes the redundant preposition before ‘tomorrow morning’; c correctly requires bare ‘follow’ after will. ‘Follow up on’ itself is valid in a.

criteria.prompt: Role or purpose differs meaningfully from the source; not merely rewriting it.
criteria.evidence: Sol: q5 changes hotel receptionist/night team duties into a school charity volunteer leaving work with a classmate; the message recipient, items and purpose are substantively different. Luna: Reading is a hotel receptionist handing records to the night shift; transfer changes to a school charity-fair volunteer handing items/work to a classmate.

criteria.prompt: Model answer is idiomatic and uses target; checklist is usable; writing is not automatically graded.
criteria.evidence: Sol: The three-sentence model naturally uses will hand over with ticket box/sales list and to you. The checklist verifies length, transfer meaning and changed role/situation. Self-assessment is explicit; no automatic writing/CEFR score is claimed. Luna: The three-sentence model naturally uses ‘hand over … to you’; checklist checks length, phrase use and changed role/situation. Prompt says self-assess, with no automatic grade.
